old.name: Sal de Tavira — Rui Simeão & Marisol
old.label: SALT
old.hook: Flor de Sal DOP since EU Reg. 1168/2013 · borboleta-skimmed June–September
old.text: Flor de Sal DOP since EU Reg. 1168/2013 · borboleta-skimmed June–September The Ria Formosa salt pans run roughly 60 km between Tavira and Castro Marim. Rui Simeão / Tavira Sal is the small-batch hand-skimmed Tavira producer; Marisol draws from both Ria Formosa and the Sapal de Castro Marim reserve, certified organic (EU PT-BIO-04), IFS, Kosher. King Afonso III claimed Tavira's salinas for the Portuguese Crown in 1266; the DOP was registered EU-wide on 7 November 2013. Flor de sal is hand-skimmed with the borboleta , the traditional butterfly-shaped wooden tool, between June and September only. Where Tavira & Castro Marim salt pans Address Salinas de Tavira / Castro Marim

old.name: Morgado do Quintão (Lagoa)
old.label: WINE — ORGANIC
old.hook: Family since 1810 · Algarve's largest certified-organic vineyard
old.text: Family since 1810 · Algarve's largest certified-organic vineyard Filipe Caldas de Vasconcellos's family property — vineyard history back to the 17th century, the family present since 1810. The first modern vintage was 2016; production has grown from 2,000 to 20,000 bottles. Now the Algarve's largest certified-organic vineyard, with consultant Joana Maçanita driving low-intervention, regenerative viticulture. Flagship: a monovarietal Crato Branco , dry-farmed, the canonical Algarve white. Has won "Best Wine in Portugal – Algarve" (Revista de Vinhos) two years running. Farmstay on the estate; tastings under a 2,000-year-old olive tree. Where between Silves and Lagoa — 45 min from Faro Address Estrada das Relíquias, between Silves and Lagoa

old.name: Cabrita Wines (Silves)
old.label: WINE — NEGRA MOLE
old.hook: "Queen Grape of the Algarve" — Negra Mole monovarietals
old.text: "Queen Grape of the Algarve" — Negra Mole monovarietals José André Cabrita planted Crato Branco, Manteúdo, Negra Mole and Castelão at Quinta da Vinha (Silves) in 1977; his son José Manuel runs it now. The modern winery built after 2000; first bottled vintage c. 2007. ~70,000 bottles annually across eight labels and 16 ha across three properties. The region's most prominent champion of Negra Mole, released as monovarietal across rosé, light red, sparkling, orange. The estate also hosts smaller local producers. old.name: Olhão — fishing port + 1916 market
old.label: TOWN
old.hook: 10 km east · 15 min by train · the cubic-white Bairro dos Pescadores
old.text: 10 km east · 15 min by train · the cubic-white Bairro dos Pescadores The largest fishing port of the Algarve, distinctive Moorish-influenced cubic white architecture. Twin red-brick market halls (1916, neo-Arabic green domes). The Bairro dos Pescadores behind: tight alleys, flat-roofed cube houses, women drying fish on balconies. Ferries to Armona and Culatra islands from the waterfront. Best Saturday morning before 09:00.

old.name: Tavira — the eastern Algarve's elegance
old.label: TOWN
old.hook: 35 km east · 35 min by train · 37 churches in the old town
old.text: 35 km east · 35 min by train · 37 churches in the old town The most elegant town in the eastern Algarve, bisected by the Gilão river with its seven-arched Roman bridge. The hilltop castle gardens, the Igreja de Santa Maria do Castelo (restored by Fabri after 1755), an Islamic-and-Roman urban fabric. Surviving Moorish nora (water-raising wheel) near Rua de Santo Estêvão. Sunset at the Quatro Águas jetty where the Gilão meets the lagoon, with the salt pans across the water.
